DEST.name: Kashmir
DEST.best: Mar–Jun for gardens, Dec–Feb for snow
DEST.about: Kashmir is shikara rides on Dal Lake at dawn, the Mughal gardens in full bloom, and pine valleys that turn white every winter. Stay on a heritage houseboat, ride the Gulmarg Gondola to Apharwat Peak, and follow the Lidder river through Pahalgam's meadows.
hl: Shikara ride and houseboat stay on Dal Lake
Gulmarg Gondola — one of Asia's highest cable cars
Betaab, Aru and Chandanwari valleys in Pahalgam
Mughal gardens: Nishat, Shalimar and Chashme Shahi

DEST.name: Himachal Pradesh
DEST.about: From the colonial Mall Road of Shimla to the cafés of Old Manali and the apple orchards of Kullu, Himachal is India's favourite mountain escape. Drive the Atal Tunnel to Sissu, paraglide over Solang and walk the riverside trails of Kasol.
hl: The Ridge and Mall Road, Shimla

DEST.name: Spiti Valley
DEST.about: A cold desert at 12,500 ft, Spiti is a road trip through monasteries, fossil villages and the turquoise Chandratal lake. Group departures run through the summer road season when both Kunzum and the Kinnaur route are open.
hl: Key Monastery above the Spiti river
Langza fossil village and Buddha statue

DEST.name: Ladakh
DEST.about: Ladakh rewards the slow traveller: acclimatise in Leh, cross Khardung La into the Nubra dunes, and watch Pangong Tso change colour through the day. Every itinerary builds in a rest day at altitude.

DEST.name: Uttarakhand
DEST.about: Rishikesh rafting, Mussoorie's Camel's Back Road, the lakes of Nainital and the Char Dham shrines — Uttarakhand mixes adventure, hill stations and pilgrimage within a few hours' drive.
hl: Ganga Aarti at Har Ki Pauri, Haridwar
Nainital lake and Snow View Point

DEST.name: Uttar Pradesh
DEST.about: See the Taj Mahal at sunrise, the evening Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat, and the newly built Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir in Ayodhya. Uttar Pradesh holds India's best-known monument and its oldest living city.
hl: Ganga Aarti and sunrise boat ride, Varanasi
Sarnath, where the Buddha first taught

DEST.name: Rajasthan
DEST.about: Forts on every ridge, lake palaces and a desert that glows at sunset. Rajasthan's classic circuit covers Jaipur's Pink City, Jodhpur's blue lanes, the golden fort of Jaisalmer and romantic Udaipur.
hl: Amer Fort and Hawa Mahal, Jaipur
Camel safari and desert camp at Sam dunes

DEST.name: Kerala
DEST.about: Tea estates in Munnar, spice plantations in Thekkady, and a night on a private houseboat through the Alleppey backwaters. Kerala is slow travel at its best, with Ayurveda and Kathakali along the way.
hl: Munnar tea gardens and Eravikulam National Park
Fort Kochi and Chinese fishing nets

DEST.name: Coorg & Ooty
DEST.about: Misty coffee estates in Coorg and the toy train of the Nilgiri Mountain Railway in Ooty. A gentle hill holiday for families and couples, with Mysore Palace on the way.
hl: Abbey Falls and Raja's Seat, Coorg

DEST.name: South India
DEST.about: Combine the Dravidian temple towns of Tamil Nadu with the hill stations and backwaters of Kerala. Ideal for a longer first trip south.

DEST.name: Madurai & Rameswaram
DEST.about: Pray at the Meenakshi Amman Temple, walk Rameswaram's thousand-pillared corridors and ride the Pamban bridge across the sea to Dhanushkodi.

DEST.name: Tirupati
DEST.about: A darshan-focused package with special entry assistance, stay at Tirupati and visits to Padmavathi Ammavari Temple and Srikalahasti.

DEST.name: Puri & Odisha
DEST.about: Darshan at Shree Jagannath Temple, the Sun Temple at Konark and dolphin spotting on Chilika Lake, all within a short drive of Bhubaneswar.

DEST.name: Sikkim & Darjeeling
DEST.about: Sunrise over Kanchenjunga from Tiger Hill, the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, and Gangtok's MG Marg. Add Tsomgo Lake and Nathula Pass for high-altitude views.

DEST.name: Arunachal Pradesh
DEST.about: Tawang Monastery, Sela Pass at 13,700 ft and the Dirang valley. Indian travellers need an Inner Line Permit, which we arrange for you.

DEST.name: Andaman
DEST.about: Radhanagar Beach on Havelock (Swaraj Dweep), coral reefs off Neil Island and the Light & Sound show at the Cellular Jail. Ferries between islands are included.
hl: Scuba and snorkelling at Elephant Beach

DEST.name: Goa
DEST.about: North Goa's beaches and shacks, the churches of Old Goa, and the quiet coves of the south. Add water sports, a sunset cruise on the Mandovi or a spice farm lunch.
hl: Palolem and Cola beach in the south

DEST.name: Maharashtra
DEST.about: The Gateway of India and Marine Drive, darshan at Shirdi Sai Baba Samadhi Mandir, the caves of Ajanta and Ellora, and monsoon weekends in Lonavala and Mahabaleshwar.
hl: Gateway of India and Marine Drive

DEST.name: Dwarka & Somnath
DEST.about: Dwarkadhish Temple on the Gomti ghats, Bet Dwarka by boat, Nageshwar Jyotirlinga and the seaside Somnath Jyotirlinga with its evening light show.
hl: Somnath Temple and Light & Sound show

DEST.name: Ujjain & Omkareshwar
DEST.about: Attend the Bhasma Aarti at Mahakaleshwar (subject to booking), walk the Mahakal Lok corridor and take a boat around Omkareshwar island.

DEST.name: Char Dham
DEST.about: The Char Dham Yatra visits four Himalayan shrines between May and early November. We handle registration, hotels near each Dham and helicopter options for Kedarnath.

DEST.name: Varanasi & Ayodhya
DEST.about: Two of India's holiest cities in one trip: Kashi Vishwanath, the ghats of Varanasi and Ayodhya's Ram Mandir, Hanuman Garhi and Saryu Aarti.
hl: Saryu Aarti at Ram ki Paidi

DEST.name: Thailand
DEST.about: Phi Phi and James Bond Island from Phuket, Pattaya's Coral Island, and Bangkok's Grand Palace and floating markets. Visa-free entry for Indian passport holders (check current rules before travel).
hl: Grand Palace and Wat Arun, Bangkok

DEST.name: Bali
DEST.about: Rice terraces in Ubud, the lake temple of Ulun Danu Beratan, cliff-top Uluwatu at sunset and a private pool villa for honeymooners.

DEST.name: Maldives
DEST.about: Speedboat or seaplane to your island resort, snorkel the house reef and dine on the sand. Free visa on arrival for Indian travellers.

DEST.name: Dubai
DEST.about: Burj Khalifa's At the Top, a desert safari with BBQ dinner, the Dhow cruise at Marina and a day in Abu Dhabi for the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque.

DEST.name: Singapore & Malaysia
DEST.about: Gardens by the Bay, Sentosa and Universal Studios in Singapore, then the Petronas Towers, Batu Caves and Genting Highlands in Malaysia.

DEST.name: Bhutan
DEST.about: Hike to Tiger's Nest monastery, cross Dochula pass and see Punakha Dzong at the river confluence. Indian travellers need no visa, only an entry permit and the Sustainable Development Fee.

DEST.name: Japan
DEST.about: Tokyo, Mt Fuji, Kyoto and Osaka by bullet train. Cherry blossom departures in spring and autumn foliage tours in November.

DEST.name: Vietnam
DEST.about: Overnight cruise in Ha Long Bay, the Golden Bridge at Ba Na Hills and the lantern-lit old town of Hoi An.

DEST.name: Europe
DEST.about: London, Paris, Switzerland and Italy on escorted group tours with Indian meals, or tailor-made for couples and families.

DEST.name: Australia
DEST.about: Sydney Opera House, the Great Ocean Road, and the Great Barrier Reef from Cairns. Couple departures include reef cruises and a Gold Coast theme park day.

DEST.name: Bahrain
DEST.about: A short-haul Gulf break: Bahrain Fort, the Tree of Life, marinas and the Formula 1 circuit at Sakhir.

DEST.name: Nepal
DEST.about: Kathmandu's Durbar Squares, Pashupatinath, a mountain flight past Everest and lakeside Pokhara. No visa for Indian citizens.

DEST.name: Mauritius
DEST.about: Île aux Cerfs, the seven-coloured earth of Chamarel and the underwater waterfall viewpoint of Le Morne. Visa-free for Indian passport holders.

DEST.name: Meghalaya
DEST.about: Meghalaya is waterfalls that drop off green cliffs, living root bridges built by Khasi villages over centuries, and the crystal-clear Umngot river at Dawki. Base yourself in Shillong and Cherrapunjee (Sohra), walk to Nongriat's double-decker root bridge, and end in Mawlynnong, often called Asia's cleanest village.
hl: Double-decker living root bridge at Nongriat
Boating on the clear Umngot river at Dawki
Nohkalikai, Seven Sisters and Wei Sawdong falls
Mawlynnong village and the Sky View bamboo tower

DEST.name: Sri Lanka
DEST.about: Sri Lanka packs ancient rock fortresses, tea country and palm-fringed beaches into a small island. Climb Sigiriya at sunrise, see the Temple of the Tooth in Kandy, take the blue train through the hills to Ella, and finish on the south-west coast at Bentota or Galle.
hl: Sigiriya rock fortress and Dambulla cave temples
Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic, Kandy
Scenic train ride from Nuwara Eliya to Ella
Nine Arch Bridge and Little Adam's Peak
Beach time and Galle Fort on the south coast

DEST.name: Georgia
DEST.about: Georgia sits where Europe meets Asia: cobbled old-town Tbilisi with sulphur baths, the Gergeti Trinity Church under Mount Kazbek, wine villages of Kakheti and the Black Sea at Batumi. Indian passport holders can apply for an e-visa.
hl: Old Tbilisi, Narikala Fortress and sulphur baths
Gergeti Trinity Church below Mount Kazbek
Ananuri Fortress and the Georgian Military Road
Batumi boulevard on the Black Sea

DEST.name: Kazakhstan (Almaty)
DEST.about: Almaty is a green city at the foot of the Tian Shan mountains, and an easy visa-free trip for Indians (check current rules). Ride up to Shymbulak, see the turquoise Big Almaty Lake, and drive out to Charyn Canyon and the Kolsai lakes.
hl: Kok Tobe hill and Almaty's bazaars

DEST.name: Kenya (Masai Mara)
DEST.best: Jul–Oct for the migration; Jan–Mar dry season
DEST.about: The Masai Mara is East Africa's classic safari: open grassland with lion, cheetah, elephant and, from July to October, the wildebeest migration and its river crossings. Combine game drives with Lake Naivasha and a night in Nairobi.
hl: Morning and evening game drives in the Masai Mara
Great Migration river crossings (Jul–Oct, not guaranteed)

GUIDES.title: Visa-free and visa-on-arrival countries for Indian travellers
GUIDES.intro: Short-haul international trips are easiest when the paperwork is light. These are the destinations where Indian passport holders can usually travel without applying for a visa in advance.
body: Visa-free destinations

Nepal and Bhutan need no visa for Indian citizens (Bhutan charges a daily Sustainable Development Fee and issues an entry permit). Thailand, Malaysia and Mauritius have offered visa-free entry for tourist stays under recent schemes.
Visa on arrival and e-visa

The Maldives gives a free 30-day visa on arrival. Indonesia (Bali) offers visa on arrival and e-VOA. Vietnam runs an online e-visa. The UAE and Bahrain offer e-visas, with visa on arrival for eligible travellers holding certain visas.
What you still need
A passport valid for at least six months, confirmed return tickets, hotel bookings and proof of funds. Some countries ask for travel insurance and an arrival card filled online.
Rules change often
Visa schemes are extended, changed or withdrawn at short notice. Always confirm with the embassy or our visa desk before you book flights.

GUIDES.title: Char Dham Yatra: how to plan your trip
GUIDES.intro: The Char Dham Yatra visits Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath and Badrinath in the Garhwal Himalaya. Here is how to plan it without stress.
body: When the temples open
The shrines open between late April and May and close around Diwali and Bhai Dooj in October–November. May–June and September–October are the best windows; July–August brings monsoon landslides.
Order of the yatra
The traditional route runs west to east: Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath and then Badrinath. A full yatra by road takes 10–12 days from Haridwar or Dehradun.
Registration is mandatory
Every pilgrim must register with Uttarakhand Tourism before the yatra. We complete registration for everyone in your booking.
Kedarnath trek or helicopter
Kedarnath is about 16 km on foot from Gaurikund. Ponies, palkis and helicopter shuttles are available. Helicopter seats sell out fast, so book as soon as the portal opens.
Fitness and health
Walk daily for a few weeks before the yatra. Senior travellers should get a medical check-up and carry regular medicines, warm layers and rain gear.

GUIDES.title: Best time to visit Kashmir, month by month
GUIDES.intro: Kashmir looks different in every season. Pick your month based on what you want to see.
body: March to May: spring
Tulip Garden in Srinagar blooms from late March to April. Pleasant days, cool nights and the Mughal gardens at their best.
June to August: summer
Ideal for Pahalgam, Sonamarg and long valley drives. The busiest season, so book houseboats early.
September to November: autumn
Chinar trees turn gold and red, skies are clear and crowds are thinner. Great for photography.
December to February: winter
Snow in Gulmarg and Pahalgam, skiing and snowmobile rides. Some roads close after heavy snowfall; keep a buffer day.

GUIDES.title: Ladakh acclimatisation: stay safe at high altitude
GUIDES.intro: Leh sits at about 3,500 m. Most altitude problems are avoided with a simple, slow plan.
body: Rest on day one
Spend the first 24–48 hours in Leh doing nothing strenuous. All TripPartner Ladakh itineraries include this rest day.
Go up slowly
Visit Leh-area sights before crossing high passes like Khardung La and Chang La. Sleep lower than the highest point you visit where possible.
Drink water, skip alcohol
Stay hydrated and avoid alcohol and smoking for the first few days.
Know the signs

Headache, nausea, dizziness and breathlessness at rest are warning signs. Tell your driver or trip expert and descend if symptoms get worse. Consult your doctor before the trip, especially with any medical condition.

Thermal inner wear, 2–3 warm layers, a padded or down jacket, woollen cap, gloves, woollen socks and waterproof shoes with good grip.

PFAQ: Adults aged 18 and above with a verified phone number and government ID. Profiles that fail verification are not shown.
Is my phone number visible to others?
No. Your phone, email and full name stay hidden. Chat opens only after both travellers accept a request, and you can block or report anyone at any time.
Do we have to share a room?
No. Separate rooms are always available. A shared room is booked only when both travellers agree, and either of you can switch to separate rooms before the final payment.
Can one person pay for both?
Yes. One traveller can pay for both, you can split the cost 50/50 with two payment links, or each of you can book individually on the same departure.
We request adjacent seats on flights, trains and buses. Airline and railway seat allocation is subject to availability, and paid seat selection may apply.
Each traveller's booking follows our cancellation policy. If your partner cancels a shared-room booking, you can continue with a single-room supplement or change your plans.
No. Travel Partner helps adults find compatible travel companions. Respectful behaviour is mandatory and any misuse leads to removal.
PFAQ2: Why do you ask for a photo and ID proof?
A clear photo helps travellers recognise each other, and a government ID with a selfie match keeps fake profiles out. Both are checked by our team before a profile goes live.
Who can see my ID document?

Only TripPartner's verification team. Other members never see it — they only see an "ID verified" badge. ID images are deleted once your profile is approved or rejected; we keep only the ID type and last 4 digits.
